    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_ToPackage" sourceRef="GW_ParallelSplit" targetRef="Task_Package"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_ToInsuranceDecision" sourceRef="GW_ParallelSplit" targetRef="GW_InsuranceNeeded"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_InsuranceYes" name="Yes" sourceRef="GW_InsuranceNeeded" targetRef="Task_Insurance">
      <bpmn:conditionExpression xsi:type="bpmn:tFormalExpression">${insuranceNecessary == true}</bpmn:conditionExpression>
    </bpmn:sequenceFlow>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_NoInsurance" name="No" sourceRef="GW_InsuranceNeeded" targetRef="GW_InsuranceMerge"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_InsuranceToMerge" sourceRef="Task_Insurance" targetRef="GW_InsuranceMerge"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_InsuranceMergeToJoin" sourceRef="GW_InsuranceMerge" targetRef="GW_ParallelJoin"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_LabelToJoin" sourceRef="Task_WriteLabel" targetRef="GW_ParallelJoin"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_PackageToJoin" sourceRef="Task_Package" targetRef="GW_ParallelJoin"/>

    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_JoinToPickup" sourceRef="GW_ParallelJoin" targetRef="Task_PrepareForPickup"/>
    <bpmn:sequenceFlow id="Flow_PickupToEnd" sourceRef="Task_PrepareForPickup" targetRef="End_ReadyForPickup"/>

  </bpmn:process>

rules.instruction: When the description states a decision whose alternative branches later converge again before a shared activity or end event: Model the decision as an exclusive gateway split with labeled outgoing flows for each alternative. Join the alternative branches with a separate exclusive gateway merge placed immediately before the shared activity or end event. Do not route the alternative branches with direct sequence flows into one shared element, and do not drop the merge or the split.
rules.situation: the description states that, after a decision, one activity is always performed and a second activity is performed alongside it only if a stated condition holds, and both then lead to the same next step

rules.instruction: When the description states that an activity may optionally be carried out (for example 'may also conduct' an activity), with no condition beyond the team's own choice, and the process continues with a shared step afterwards: Model the optional activity as one branch of an exclusive gateway split, with a labeled bypass flow that skips it. Connect the end of the optional activity and the bypass flow into a separate exclusive gateway merge placed before the shared step. Do not link the optional activity directly to the following step, and do not omit the split or the merge.
rules.situation: the description states two or more activities that each take place only if needed (for example 'if necessary'), so that any subset of them, including none or all, may occur, and the process continues with a shared step after them

rules.instruction: When the description states that one activity is performed only if a stated condition holds, while another activity always happens alongside it, and both branches must rejoin before a later step: Model the conditional activity and the always-performed activity as the two outgoing branches of an inclusive gateway split: guard the conditional branch with its condition and leave the always-performed branch unconditional, so both can proceed when the condition holds. Rejoin the branches with an inclusive gateway join before the next step. Place both gateways in the lane of the role that makes the decision or performs the branching, and do not replace the split with an exclusive gateway, which would send the flow down only one branch.
rules.situation: the description states that one activity is performed only if a stated condition holds, while another activity always happens alongside it, and both branches must rejoin before a later step

rules.instruction: When the description states an action performed by a participant and then names a later action or decision as the next step, whether inside a conditional branch or in the main sequence, so that the later element depends on the earlier one: Model each such action as its own task, and connect its outgoing sequence flow directly to the next task or gateway that the description places after it, within the same branch. Do not leave the action without an outgoing flow, and do not route its flow to a different element, such as a gateway or task placed elsewhere, when the description ties the next step to it.
rules.situation: the description states an action performed by a participant and then names a later action or decision as the next step, whether inside a conditional branch or in the main sequence, so that the later element depends on the earlier one

rules.instruction: When the description opens with a conditional clause ('If ...') that decides whether the whole process runs, and no external message, signal, time or condition is what starts it: Model a plain start event labelled with the situation named in that opening condition, placed before the first gateway or parallel split, and connect it in sequence to the first step that the condition gates. Do not leave the gating condition out of the start, and do not attach it to a later gateway as if the process had already started.
rules.situation: the description opens with a conditional clause ('If ...') that decides whether the whole process runs, and no external message, signal, time or condition is what starts it

rules.instruction: When the description states that one participant sends requests for proposals to several outside parties and then chooses one of them, and does not state that those parties run their own processes or act as independent participants in the interaction: Model the outreach to the outside parties and the later choice of one of them as tasks and a decision inside the lane of the participant who performs them. Do not create a pool for those outside parties, and do not add message flows to or from them, unless the description states that they act as independent participants with their own behaviour.
rules.situation: the description states that one participant sends requests for proposals to several outside parties and then chooses one of them, and does not state that those parties run their own processes or act as independent participants in the interaction

rules.instruction: When the description states a decision whose outcome determines a second decision or an activity that depends on it (for example, one choice leads to a further choice on a different criterion), and the branches of the first decision lead into that next element: Model each case of the first decision as an outgoing branch of an exclusive gateway, and connect every such branch to the next element it leads to, which may be a second gateway or an activity. Route alternative branches that reach a common later element through an exclusive merge placed just before it. Do not leave a gateway's branch unconnected, and do not skip a gateway's outcome by connecting one decision directly to an activity that the description places after another decision.
rules.situation: the description states a decision whose outcome determines a second decision or an activity that depends on it (for example, one choice leads to a further choice on a different criterion), and the branches of the first decision lead into that next element

rules.instruction: When the description states that an activity can already be carried out while a later activity waits for a stated readiness or completion condition, so the later activity follows only once that condition holds: Model an exclusive gateway between the preparatory activity and the gated activity. Place it in the lane of the role that checks the condition. Give the flow to the gated activity the stated condition, and give the alternative flow a label and its own next step, such as a wait or return to the check. Do not connect the preparatory activity directly to the gated activity, which would let the later step run without the condition.
rules.situation: the description states that an activity can already be carried out while a later activity waits for a stated readiness or completion condition, so the later activity follows only once that condition holds

rules.instruction: When the description names several internal roles of one organization that each carry out activities, and at least one role's activity is conditional (for example 'if necessary'), so the role acts only in some cases: Model the organization as one pool and give each internal role its own lane inside that pool, including a role whose only activity is conditional. Place the conditional activity as a task in that role's lane, behind an exclusive gateway with a branch that skips it. Do not drop the lane or move the activity into another role's lane because the activity may not occur.
rules.situation: the description names several internal roles of one organization that each carry out activities, and at least one role's activity is conditional (for example 'if necessary'), so the role acts only in some cases
